name: Being Worried
overview: Scripture teaches that being worried stems from relying on our own understanding rather than fully trusting in the Lord, as Proverbs 3:5 urges us to do. Jesus instructs believers not to be anxious about daily needs like food and clothing, emphasizing that life is more valuable than these concerns and that worry cannot add any measure to our lives (Matthew 6:25, 27). Instead, we are called to seek God's kingdom and righteousness first, with the assurance that all necessary things will be provided (Matthew 6:33). We are reminded to focus on the present day without being burdened by the uncertainties of tomorrow, trusting God’s provision and timing (Matthew 6:34). Encouragement and uplifting words can also counteract heaviness of heart, offering gladness where worry might otherwise cause us to stoop (Proverbs 12:25).
